reading: The empty interior of the grey square outline is split into four 2x2 quadrants filled as a checkerboard of the two outside marker colours: the quadrant nearest each marker takes that marker's colour, and the diagonally opposite quadrant takes the same colour.

slots.region: interior of the one rectangular outline (frame), cut into four equal quadrants
slots.colours: the two isolated marker cells outside the frame
slots.assignment: quadrant nearest a marker gets its colour; diagonal quadrant same; the other two quadrants get the other marker colour

why: every interior cell is filled; frame and markers unchanged

reading: A key strip of coloured columns gives a top-to-bottom colour order; the one shape (already present in some of those colours, stacked vertically) is copied above/below in the missing key colours so the stack follows the key order, and the key strip is erased.

slots.key: the multi-coloured strip of vertical one-colour bars (left-to-right order = top-to-bottom order)
slots.unit: the repeated shape (all present copies identical up to colour)
slots.placement: copies stacked flush vertically, same columns as existing copies, one per key colour in key order

why: the output column stack reads the key colours in order, every copy the same shape

reading: Four coloured cells sit in the inner corners of a rectangular outline; each is removed and placed at the cell just diagonally outside the opposite outer corner of the outline (inner top-left goes to outer bottom-right, etc.).

slots.subject: the four single cells at the inner corners of the outline
slots.target: the cell diagonally outside the outline's opposite corner
slots.rest: inner corner cells cleared to background

why: outer corner colour = colour of the diagonally opposite inner corner; interior becomes empty

reading: The most common colour (background) stays; every other cell becomes grey 5.
why: every non-background cell becomes 5 (key a->5 for all a); background cells unchanged

reading: Each 2x2 grey block gets four single cells placed diagonally outside its corners: 1 top-left, 2 top-right, 3 bottom-left, 4 bottom-right.
why: around every grey object the same 4x4 pattern 1..2 / .55. / .55. / 3..4 appears; all else unchanged

reading: A lattice of grey separator lines is cluttered with noise cells of one colour; the noise is erased, the separator lines are restored to full grey, and every crossing of two separator lines is painted the noise colour.

slots.lines: the (mostly) full rows and columns of grey 5
slots.noise: all cells of the one non-grey foreground colour
slots.marks: intersections of separator rows and columns get the noise colour
slots.rest: everything else becomes background or grey line

why: output = clean separator lattice with crossings in the noise colour

reading: The grid is doubled in width and the horizontal periodic pattern in the coloured rows is continued across the new width.

slots.size: output width = 2 x input width, same height

why: every output row is the input row's periodic continuation

reading: On a lattice of hollow 3x3 squares, two cells of the same colour mark opposite corners of a block of squares; a rectangle of that colour is drawn along the gap lines enclosing that block, and the centre of each enclosed square is filled with the colour.

slots.markers: pairs of same-coloured cells lying on gap rows/columns
slots.rectangle: the gap-line outline of the smallest block of squares spanned by the pair
slots.fill: centre cell of each square inside the rectangle

why: each marker pair yields one outline on gap lines plus coloured centres; other squares unchanged

reading: Each single coloured cell in the top row drops a vertical line of its colour to the bottom border, crossing every block; where the line crosses a block of its own colour it is drawn in the background colour instead.

slots.source: the single non-background cells in the top row
slots.line: the full column below each source, to the bottom border
slots.colour: source colour, except background colour inside blocks of the same colour

why: each source column becomes its colour everywhere except inside same-colour blocks, where it becomes background

reading: The left panel holds small shapes on rows; they are redrawn on the same rows in the empty right panel: shapes touching the left margin stay at the left margin, shapes touching the right margin go to the right margin, and shapes spanning the full width are stretched to the full width.

slots.source: the left panel interior (with its one-cell margin)
slots.target: the empty right panel interior, same rows
slots.rule: keep shape width and align to left or right inner margin; full-width bars stretch to full inner width

why: each source row's shapes appear on the same row of the target panel with matching edge alignment
